reasoning_traces.think:
The study applies mixed-effects modeling to estimate subway ridership changes due to weather, with fixed effects for boroughs and random intercepts per OD pair. The model uses PCA to reduce weather covariates into interpretable components. Key findings show that gust speed negatively impacts ridership, especially in Manhattan, and that December’s apparent effect vanishes when gusts are controlled for. This suggests a confounding relationship between seasonal trends and gust intensity. The model assumes linearity and temporal stationarity but lacks predictive validation and suffers from high residual variance. Its methodological similarity to GSI's prior work (ledger 1703) and lack of real-world application make it unsuitable for GSE integration despite its formal rigor.
